title: Graceful cross-boundary quota handoff for reserved monthly->daily windows
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a robust handoff mechanism that cleanly migrates reserved-capacity quota state between monthly anchored allocations and daily/rolling sub-windows. The goal is to avoid over- and under-counts during boundary crossings (month->day, DST transitions, tenant timezone migrations) while preserving predictable throttling and correct billing signals.

Background: Customers on reserved plans purchase monthly token/throughput budgets, but our runtime enforces per-request and per-day limits to protect shared resources. Current reset logic can cause small but recurring double-dips (temporary double-counting) or missed replenishments when month boundary events align with daily reset windows or when tenants are moved between pools. Those discrepancies surface as incorrect throttling, sudden failure spikes after rollovers, and billing reconciliation tickets.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic, idempotent handoff from monthly anchor to daily rolling windows for reserved tenants.
- Ensure no transient overdraw results in customer-visible 429s immediately after boundary.
- Produce audit-friendly telemetry and ledger entries for any adjustments performed during handoff.
- Keep runtime performance overhead minimal and avoid blocking request paths.

Proposed approach:
1) Lease-based handoff coordinator: introduce a lightweight coordinator per-reserved-tenant that obtains a short-lived lease around the boundary. The lease serializes the handoff so only one worker performs reconciliation for a tenant at a time. Lease metadata: tenant_id, anchor_timestamp, pre_handoff_snapshot_id.
2) Delta-driven credit movement: compute deltas between monthly pool ledger and daily subwindows using existing snapshot mechanism. Move credits by emitting an explicit transfer ledger event rather than rewriting consumption history. This keeps audit trails intact.
3) Grace buffer window: when handoff occurs, temporarily allow a configurable micro-burst buffer (e.g., 2% of monthly allocation or X tokens capped) for the tenant until the handoff finalizes to avoid immediate 429s. The buffer is reconciled and removed as part of the transfer event.
4) Idempotency & monotonic checkpointing: every handoff produces a monotonic checkpoint token that the coordinator persists; replays detect completed handoffs and are NOP.
5) Telemetry and alerts: emit metrics for handoff_duration_ms, credits_transferred, buffer_used_tokens, and handshake_retries. Create alert if handoff_duration_ms > 10s or if buffer_used_tokens > 50% of configured buffer.

Acceptance criteria:
- Handoff path reduces post-boundary 429 spikes for reserved tenants by >95% in staging replay.
- Ledger shows a single transfer event per tenant per boundary; no overlapping transfer events are created when retries occur.
- End-to-end tests covering normal boundary, DST jump, tenant pool migration, and simulated coordinator preemption all pass.
- Production rollout includes a toggleable feature flag and graceful kill-switch.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We choose transfer events over rewriting history to preserve billing auditability at the cost of a slightly more complex ledger model.
- The micro-burst buffer trades temporary additional capacity risk for reduced customer-visible errors; buffer size must be conservative and guarded by alerts.
- Coordinator lease duration should be short (e.g., 30s) and auto-extend only if progress is observed to bound contention.

Rollout plan:
- Step 1 (staging): integrate coordinator and delta-transfer logic behind feature flag; run daily replay for last 30 days on staging tenants. Monitor metrics. (2d)
- Step 2 (canary prod): enable for 1% of reserved tenants selected by low-utilization and high observability. Run for 48h. (3d)
- Step 3 (broader ramp): 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with telemetry thresholds gating each step. Provide runbook for rollback.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for ledger transfer emission and idempotency token handling.
- Integration test that simulates concurrent handoff attempts (race) and verifies single transfer event.
- Chaos test: kill coordinator mid-handoff and validate retry path is safe.
- Load test for performance impact: ensure <1% p95 latency increase on request path.

Telemetry / dashboards:
- New Grafana dashboard: Billing/Handoff Overview showing handoff_rate, handoff_success_ratio, average_credits_transferred, buffer_consumption_pct.
- Log link format in events for quick drilldowns: https://console.redwoodinc/ledgers/{{tenant}}/transfers

Related artifacts / links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwoodinc/space/BILLING/pages/12032-cross-boundary-handoff
- Proto PR: https://github.com/redwoodinc/platform/pull/4382
- Ledger schema changes: https://github.com/redwoodinc/ledger/commit/5f3e1a2

Notes:
- Coordinate with Billing Eng team and Legal for auditability language before GA.
- Consider follow-up to support hourly-anchored customers if this design proves stable.
